followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the intentional late-2017 Dehiba–Wazen restriction observations, distinguishing protest barriers from checkpoint decisions to protect travellers. Direct crossing restrictions support inclusion despite uncertain continuity. Retain the source-specific restriction on Libyan vehicles entering Tunisia and broader ordinary passage, with returning nationals and some women without goods excepted. Different actors’ road and checkpoint actions are not merged into uniform all-traffic enforcement. Keep unknown onset/end and the 6 December confirmation held without a numeric duration. The removed November road barrier, differing retrospective durations and prospective 7 December return do not establish one continuous interval or observed endpoint. Retain Trade and protectionism / Trade and transport protests for the seized-goods grievance, and Security / Public order and immediate safety for the mayor’s separate protection explanation. Neither validates alleged wrongdoing by customs. The broadcaster’s mayor interview, TAP-derived Tunisian reports and Al Wasat’s attributed Al Arab account have distinct or shared origins explicitly identified. Undated publication and prospective wording remain limits; repeated TAP accounts are not independent confirmations. Retain unlocated Dehiba–Wazen crossing and approach text, with null coordinates. Removed barriers, threats and checkpoint restrictions need separate geographic resolution before any precise map binding.
